response.markdown_report:
At 10% progress, prioritize **diverse-timescale initialization of the existing GRU update gate**, conditional on execution consistency. Retain GRU4Rec and add a mean-retention-matched initialization control.

Three starting-point insights guide this choice. Embedding-conditioned retention could suppress isolated historical interests, but unavailable temporal measurements provide no supporting evidence. An additional gate attenuates already-gated memory, making existing-gate initialization a simpler first experiment. All categories fail final-feature consistency, despite zero aligned-feature and candidate-score discrepancies; this localizes investigation without identifying the cause.

Three literature insights refine the experiment. Chrono initialization [1] links gate biases to nominal retention horizons, not guaranteed nonlinear memory lifetimes. minGRU [2] supports studying coordinate-wise retention, while replacing GRU4Rec remains outside scope. ICSRec [3] motivates subsequence supervision, but agreement objectives can erase changing intent.

The framework separates **execution**, **memory allocation**, and **supervision**. Shared readout semantics support interpretable diagnostics; gate initialization changes initial retention; auxiliary losses impose invariances. Execution verification precedes every direction.

Scores below are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each dimension includes a positive and negative reason.

| Proposal | Scores | Positive / negative assessment by dimension |
|---|---|---|
| Existing-gate timescales [1], selected | 3/7/7/6/3 | O: focused adaptation / established method; P: inexpensive foundation / gains uncertain; U: balances recent and persistent evidence / no intent labels; M: controlled memory hypothesis / initialization cannot fix execution; D: few parameter edits / integration and controls require care |
| Additional retention gate [2] | 4/6/7/5/5 | O: explicit conditioning / gating precedent; P: adaptive forgetting / redundant attenuation; U: targets stale influence and weak recent fit / may erase lasting preferences; M: testable retention / temporal evidence absent; D: small module / parity and throughput costs |
| Same-endpoint subsequence consistency [3] | 4/6/6/5/4 | O: cautious augmentation / established supervision; P: robustness / intent mixing; U: repeated evidence / broad associations may persist; M: alternative regularization / training separation already strong; D: shared weights / additional forwards |

The selected experiment targets **isolated older interests persisting** and **recent, repeated behavior receiving insufficient priority**. Different initial retention horizons could balance these needs, without establishing compatibility, mood, or satisfied demand. Its mandatory execution work addresses the measured final-feature failure; initialization alone does not.

Compare baseline, heterogeneous horizons, and uniform bias matching heterogeneous mean bias-only retention. Preserve reset-gate initialization. First compare readouts from the same forward result, then isolate transformations, padding, batch shape, and predictor serialization. Keep existing tolerances and temporal results unavailable until checks pass.

Prespecify checkpoints, budget, and ties. Select by official four-category macro validation HR@10; sampled-candidate rankings need not match full-catalog rankings [4]. Where available, report paired user-hit differences and conditional bootstrap intervals. Limited queries reduce discretion, but checkpoint selection still creates optimism [5]. No improvement is claimed.

References: [1] https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.11188; [2] https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.01201; [3] https://doi.org/10.1145/3616855.3635773; [4] https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/; [5] https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html

idea.description: Initialize the corrected GRU4Rec's existing update-gate coordinates across short and longer nominal retention horizons, without adding gates or changing its backbone. Compare against the corrected baseline and a uniform initialization matching mean bias-only retention. Establish consistent final-feature extraction across the actual model, ModelView, and embedded predictor before interpreting temporal diagnostics.
idea.motivation: The user diagnosis identifies stale isolated interests and insufficient priority for recent repeated behavior. Diverse initial retention horizons offer a minimal hypothesis for balancing these two failures, but do not encode explicit intent, compatibility, mood, or ownership. All four categories also exhibit measured final-feature execution failures. Resolve these independently rather than crediting initialization with an execution repair. Frequency-stratified training confusion supplies a secondary descriptive outcome, especially for less frequent items; neither its improvement nor temporal usefulness follows from the proposed initialization.
idea.implementation_notes:
Extend the supplied corrected baseline rather than reconstructing unavailable training code. Preserve its loss, optimizer, sampling, dimensions, dropout, batch size, reset/candidate initialization, and all other parameter initialization. The declared changes are update-gate bias initialization and a prespecified checkpoint evaluation grid. Keep the existing baseline configuration as the priority control; do not add frozen gates, another backbone, auxiliary losses, or text features to this initial experiment.

For PyTorch's h=z*h_previous+(1-z)*candidate, use H horizons log-spaced from 2 to max(2, history_window), including endpoints. Set total update-gate bias to log(T-1), assigning this value to bias_ih[H:2H] and zero to bias_hh[H:2H], for every existing recurrent layer. Keep reset biases exactly as supplied, rather than setting them to zero or to negative update biases. This deterministic log-spaced construction is an adaptation, not the original chrono prescription, which samples T-1 uniformly over [1,T_max-1]. For the uniform control, compute z_bar=mean(1-1/T_j) and set every total update bias to logit(z_bar). This matches mean bias-only retention, not its full distribution or the expected gate activation under nonzero inputs. Leave update-gate input and recurrent weights trainable in both variants. Construct each variant with identical category-specific seed-42 baseline initialization and apply the deterministic bias edit afterward, so adding the intervention consumes no additional random draws. Never reinitialize a loaded checkpoint.

The exact isolated carry-path e-folding time is -1/log(z), approximately T for large T. Nonzero input/recurrent preactivations, candidate recurrence, and gate derivatives mean these biases do not enforce a memory lifetime. Training may erase the initialization. A heterogeneous-versus-uniform gain would support the utility of this initialization under the experiment, not establish fixed learned timescales or causal intent recovery. Frozen-gate controls are deferred because they alter the hypothesis and consume additional budget.

Before comparing initialization variants, investigate execution failures on the unchanged baseline. Capture one forward result and compare production readout with an independent maximum-nonzero-position gather from that same feature tensor. Distinguish raw GRU outputs from projected, normalized, activated, or residual-enhanced recommendation features. For a unidirectional packed GRU, the last valid raw output should correspond to top-layer h_n with original batch order restored; transformed features require the identical transformation of h_n. Check indices, transformations, initial states, and empty-row policy before attributing discrepancies to an indexing bug or numerical effects.

Do not pass left-padded histories directly to pack_padded_sequence. If packing is already used or is needed for an execution correction, compact nonzero items chronologically into a right-padded contiguous prefix, pass positive CPU lengths with enforce_sorted=False, and scatter unpacked valid outputs back to original positions. Bypass packing for empty rows; clamping a zero length to one invents a recurrent step. Otherwise preserve the baseline's masked recurrent path: freeze state on padding and return zero padded features. In the original left-padded representation always gather the maximum nonzero position, never count-1. Preserve the supplied empty-history scoring policy, including any learned item bias.

Use identical weights, inputs, evaluation mode, dtype, and initial states. Check repeated identical-shape execution before singleton versus mixed batches, added leading padding, raw recurrence versus output transforms, actual model versus ModelView, and serialized predictor agreement. Include empty, singleton, mixed-length, maximum-length, and standalone all-padding cases, plus BxLxK score references. Functional dropout must respect self.training. CPU/float64 and cuDNN-disabled runs are diagnostic controls; record absolute/relative errors and score/rank effects. PyTorch does not guarantee bitwise batched-versus-sliced equality, but this does not authorize relaxing atol=1e-5 and rtol=1e-4 or dismissing failures. Report unresolved failures and leave temporal metrics null. Any necessary execution correction must be explicit and shared by all compared configurations; do not silently repair checkpoint semantics.

Retain item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), score_candidates, family-specific sample_batch, and the host ModelView interfaces. view.model remains the actual trained nn.Module. Keep DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader) returning measured metrics and metric_definitions, and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). The diagnostic loader continues yielding (None, sequence, positive, negative), each tensor B x L. Run the existing temporal probe unchanged only after execution checks pass. Frequency-stratified margins describe sampled training separation, not validation performance or exposure. Mapped mean embedding cosine near 0.5 establishes neither diversity nor absence of low-dimensional collapse. Metadata-dependent category breakdowns remain explicitly unavailable.

Prespecify three configurations in priority order: corrected baseline, uniform matched retention, heterogeneous retention. Evaluate checkpoints only at completed epochs 10, 20, 40, 80, 120, 160, and 200. Use exactly 200 batches per completed epoch and never exceed 200 epochs. Compare configurations at checkpoint epochs completed for all four categories and all eligible configurations, preventing unequal checkpoint opportunities. Select the configuration-and-common-epoch pair maximizing official four-category macro validation HR@10; break within-configuration ties by earliest epoch and method ties by the declared priority. Each final category loads only its checkpoint from the selected configuration and epoch. This common-epoch rule explicitly replaces independent category checkpoint optimization for this experiment. Preserve host users, candidates, candidate order, and score-tie behavior; never perturb scores to break ties.

Treat the experiment list as a budget ceiling, not a promise that all fits finish. Reserve at most 3,300 GPU-seconds for each of the twelve category/configuration fits, including its validation and diagnostics, and 3,600 GPU-seconds for initial execution diagnosis and integration checks: total at most 43,200. Enforce the shared host-accounted budget, including debugging, failures, and any additional compute. Stop a fit before its cap and retain only completed scheduled checkpoints. Log every attempt and completed epoch. A configuration lacking all four category checkpoints at any scheduled epoch is ineligible. Compare eligible configurations on their common completed checkpoint grid; if no common scheduled checkpoint exists, report the comparison incomplete rather than inventing a result. Budget truncation and completed updates must accompany any exploratory comparison. No score-dependent early stopping or additional variant sweep is permitted.

If the host exposes paired per-user validation hits, report category wins b, losses c, and delta HR=(b-c)/200. One changed hit contributes 0.5 percentage points within a category and 0.125 percentage points to the four-category macro average. Use 2,000 paired bootstrap replicates with separate CPU RNG 42, resampling users within each category and averaging category differences equally; report the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles. These intervals condition on fixed models and candidates, omit training-seed variability, and do not correct adaptive checkpoint selection. Do not manufacture paired outcomes from aggregate scores. Sampled-candidate HR@10 may rank methods differently from full-catalog evaluation. Label validation gains exploratory, freeze the selected method before host held-out evaluation, and retain the simulator's separate twenty-user full-catalog procedure.

Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, and CDs_and_Vinyl routing, supplied splits, pinned evaluator, single-GPU execution, and artifacts beneath the trial directory. Each category deploys exactly one independently trained model/checkpoint, with no averaging, fusion, independent scorer, or reused other-trial checkpoint. Save architecture configuration with state_dict and update the predictor writer for any runtime readout or execution change. Verify reload and embedded-predictor agreement. No hidden test files, extra datasets, pretrained weights, unavailable reviews/ratings/categories/prices/stores, or inferred simulator traits are used. Learned initialization can still favor frequent-item shortcuts and memorize transitions; official validation and descriptive frequency slices cannot establish their absence.

originality.positive: A focused diagnosis-driven adaptation with a mean-retention-matched control distinguishes heterogeneous initialization from a general retention shift.
originality.negative: Chrono initialization and gate-bias controls are established concepts; no new recurrence or demonstrated benchmark gain is supplied.

future_potential.positive: A low-cost architectural intervention can clarify whether initial memory allocation warrants deeper study within GRU4Rec.
future_potential.negative: Training may overwrite the initialization, and ID-only recurrence cannot establish compatibility, mood, ownership needs, or generalization beyond the fixed-seed sampled-candidate setting.

code_difficulty.positive: The intervention changes existing biases without adding inference parameters, datasets, or independent predictors.
code_difficulty.negative: Faithful execution diagnosis, matched initialization, budget enforcement, checkpoint selection, and predictor consistency require more work than the bias edit itself.

related_work.title: Can recurrent neural networks warp time? — chrono initialization
contributions: Connects recurrent gating with temporal scales and motivates gate-bias initialization.
Provides the foundation for initializing existing GRU update biases; the proposed deterministic log-spaced schedule is an explicit adaptation.
limitations: Does not establish gains under the supplied four-category RecHarness protocol.
Nominal bias-only retention does not characterize the complete nonlinear model or its learned memory.
The complementary write-gate interpretation does not justify negating the GRU reset bias.

related_work.title: Were RNNs All We Needed?
contributions: Introduces simplified recurrent units with input-dependent coordinate-wise gates and parallelizable training.
Motivates studying selective retention as a contextual research direction.
limitations: Replacing GRU4Rec with minGRU would change the required backbone.
The supplied evidence does not demonstrate results on this benchmark.

related_work.title: ICSRec: Intent Contrastive Learning for Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Motivates cross-subsequence intent supervision and attention to false negatives.
limitations: Subsequence agreement can impose incorrect invariances when user intent changes.
A shared-GRU auxiliary loss requires a separately budgeted controlled experiment.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Explains limitations of sampled-candidate recommendation metrics, including disagreement with full-catalog comparisons.
limitations: Does not authorize changing the pinned evaluator or correcting its reported scores.
The selected benchmark outcome remains sampled-candidate validation HR@10.

related_work.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains how model selection can overfit finite evaluation data and bias reported performance.
limitations: Prespecification limits discretionary search but does not eliminate checkpoint-selection optimism.
Conditional paired bootstrap intervals do not automatically correct adaptive selection.

related_work.title: PyTorch GRU documentation
contributions: Specifies GRU equations, reset/update/new gate ordering, separate input/recurrent biases, sequence outputs, and final hidden states.
Supports distinguishing raw recurrent readouts from transformed recommendation features.
limitations: Documented algebra alone does not identify the observed final-feature discrepancy.
Implementation must preserve the supplied baseline's transformations and scoring semantics.

related_work.title: PyTorch pack_padded_sequence documentation
contributions: Defines packed-sequence length and ordering requirements.
Supports chronological compaction of left-padded histories before packing and restoration afterward.
limitations: Packing does not directly interpret leading padding as absent recurrent steps.
Empty histories require an explicit bypass rather than synthetic positive lengths.

related_work.title: PyTorch numerical accuracy notes
contributions: Explains why batched and sliced floating-point computations need not be bitwise identical.
Motivates controlled backend and precision comparisons when diagnosing discrepancies.
limitations: Numerical differences are a hypothesis requiring measurement.
The notes do not justify relaxing the existing diagnostic tolerances or treating failed checks as passed.
